title: Automate tenant RBAC bootstrap for Private installer (Helm + Terraform)
author: Priya Patel
description: Motivation: Private deployments require a repeatable, auditable way to bootstrap tenant-scoped RBAC roles and bindings during installer runs (VPC/on-prem). Previously teams ran ad-hoc scripts or manual kubectl steps which caused drift and onboarding delays. This PR adds an end-to-end automation path that: 1) provides a reusable Terraform module for tenant role/rolebinding/namespace creation, 2) extends the Helm-based private-installer charts with templated RBAC manifests and values to enable automatic bootstrap at install/upgrade time, and 3) adds idempotent bootstrap scripts and an e2e test harness for upgrade/rollback scenarios. Changes are intentionally backwards-compatible: the automation is opt-in via chart values and a terraform flag. Main changes: - terraform/modules/rbac: new module that creates tenant namespace, roles, rolebindings, and outputs minimal metadata required by the installer. Includes examples/variables and state locking guidance. - charts/private-installer: add templates/rbac-roles.yaml and values.rbac section to allow enabling tenant bootstrap and injecting tenant metadata produced by Terraform or an operator. - installer/scripts/bootstrap-rbac.sh: idempotent script invoked by post-install hook that validates existing roles, applies missing bindings, and writes a status ConfigMap for observability. - tests/e2e/rbac-bootstrap.test.ts: adds integration test that runs the installer in a KinD cluster, applies the terraform module output (simulated), verifies roles and bindings, performs an upgrade with role changes, and simulates a rollback to validate cleanup behavior. - docs/rbac/automation.md: onboarding docs and migration steps for customers using Private. Migration notes: - Default behavior is unchanged. To opt in, set .Values.rbac.enableBootstrap=true in the chart or set terraform variable enable_tenant_rbac=true. - When migrating existing tenants we provide a compatibility mode that will only add missing bindings and will not delete any roles unless explicit --purge flag is set. - Backups: the terraform module emits outputs suitable for cross-referencing with vault/secret managers; we recommend a snapshot before enabling purge mode. Testing: Local unit tests for helm templates, terraform fmt & validate, shellcheck for scripts, and an integration pipeline step that runs the e2e test matrix. CI initially flaked on linux-integration (timing in KinD), rerun passed. Rollout plan: - Merge to main, include in private-installer release notes. - Default off for existing clusters. Customers can enable in minor upgrade windows. - We will monitor the rbac.bootstrap.success metric and an installer-config validation alert to detect misconfigurations. Rollback: installer script is idempotent and writes a status ConfigMap so rollback will not leave half-applied bindings; the terraform module supports destroy for full removal. Security review: roles created are least-privilege scoped to tenant namespaces and reviewed by security (Lena). Related: ENG-4123 (tenant onboarding automation), SRE-208 (installer upgrade flakiness).

Add helm templates and values to private-installer for automated RBAC bootstrap
Add idempotent bootstrap script and post-install hook
Add e2e test for bootstrap + upgrade/rollback scenarios
Docs: add automation and migration guide

release_notes: Automated tenant RBAC bootstrap (Private installer): added an opt-in terraform module and helm chart support to bootstrap tenant namespaces, roles, and bindings during install/upgrade; idempotent bootstrap script and e2e tests for upgrade/rollback scenarios; default is off; see docs/rbac/automation.md for migration steps.
summary: Adds opt-in automation for tenant RBAC bootstrap across Terraform + Helm for Private installer with idempotent scripts and e2e tests; security-reviewed and backwards-compatible.
